model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, and MEMIT, with the additional method ROME also included. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^1$ to $10^3$, with tick marks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is a linear scale from 0 to 65. The data points for each method are plotted with distinct colors and markers, as indicated in the legend: Base (black, solid line, circle markers), FT (blue, dashed line, triangle markers), IKE (red, dashed line, triangle markers), MEND (brown, solid line, triangle markers), MEMIT (purple, dashed line, square markers), and ROME (green, solid line, square markers). The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 45% at a co-occurrence number of $10^1$ and decreasing to about 40% at $10^3$. The MEMIT method shows a similar trend, starting at around 40% and decreasing to approximately 35%. The MEND method starts at about 40% and decreases to around 35%. The FT and Base methods both start at approximately 35% and decrease to about 30% and 25%, respectively, at the highest co-occurrence number. The IKE method starts at about 38% and decreases to approximately 30%. Overall, all methods show a decreasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
